The biggest story around Jake Walman right now is that he's out of the lineup. His ice time had already slid to about 14 minutes a night when the Oilers scratched him, and the coverage has turned pointed: the Edmonton Journal called the situation "getting dicey," and The Hockey News wrote that the Oilers "Have Moved Beyond Sending a Message." One point in 11 games will do that.

Here's the case for patience. With Walman on the ice, Edmonton has scored 9.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve, the kind of gap that usually swings back on its own. He still has a 96.7 mph shot and top speed in the 97th percentile.

Here's the case against. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.15 more expected goals per 60 (more quality chances) with him on the ice last season, bottom 5% of defensemen, and this season Edmonton's share of chances drops with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking does credit him one defensive strength: he stops 15% of the entries aimed at him, against 11% typical. Our read: the bad luck is real, but so are the defensive problems, and both need to turn.
headline: Jake Walman is unlucky, but the Oilers aren't waiting
